openQuestions: Should the new plan REPLACE Rasd_Plan.md at the same path, or take a new name/location? This is the single decision that determines whether the restructure is a low-risk edit or a high-risk one. Keeping the path `Rasd_Plan.md` costs nothing: .prettierignore keeps protecting the Arabic tables, gate-a's IMPACT regex keeps exempting it, docs-lint and phases-sync keep resolving. Any other name requires four coordinated edits (.prettierignore, gate-a.mjs:60, docs-lint.mjs:28, phases-sync.mjs:41) plus a Constitution amendment, and the .prettierignore one is the only failure in this whole area that can turn CI red.

Is Rasd_Plan.md itself being archived, or restructured in place? The brief asks what goes into archive/previous-plans/ but does not say whether the 2209-line plan is one of them. If it is archived, §6 (the append-only contradiction register, rows 1–97) and §9 (the phase status table) must be carried forward verbatim or the two guards and the Dashboard lose their source. If it is restructured in place, only §6's row numbering and §9's six-column shape need preserving.

Does the new dashboard replace Docs/Phases/Dashboard.html at the same path, or live elsewhere? §8 item 9 makes updating that specific file a precondition for closing any phase, and phases-sync.mjs matches eight regexes against its internal HTML/JS shapes. A new dashboard at a new path leaves §8 item 9 pointing at a dead file for phases 19 onward, and leaves phases-sync guarding an orphan.

Which of the duplicated 12488b51 artifact claims is true — is it the dashboard's permanent link, or Phase 17's per-phase Artifact? §8 forbids both readings simultaneously. Whichever is wrong needs correcting in §9 before a new dashboard inherits it, because phases-sync will faithfully propagate the error and report zero drift.

Should the four governance guards (docs:lint, entrypoints:lint, phases:sync --check, gate:a) be added to CI? Today they run only on a developer's machine. That is why archiving cannot break CI — but it is also why a restructure that breaks phases-sync would go unnoticed on main until someone ran `pnpm gate:a` by hand. This is a policy question for the plan owner, not something I can resolve by measurement.

Should docs-lint.mjs be scoped to §6 as part of this work, or left as-is? It works today only because no table row outside §6 happens to start with a number >= 82 (measured: 183 numbered rows, 16 of them >= 82, all inside §6). Whether that latent trap is in scope depends on how many new tables the restructured plan introduces.

What should happen to the gitignored worktree at .claude/worktrees/agitated-cray-dd2aa8/, which holds a diverged copy of Rasd_Plan.md (86 diff lines) plus byte-identical copies of the audit, the maintenance prompt and the README? It is untracked so it cannot break anything, but it is a fourth location where a reader or an agent can find a 'plan' — and after a restructure it would be the only place the old plan still looks current.
